title: Pass a structured context object with every logger call

facts.note: Bun realization; file extension identifies JS/TS code. No restriction to production vs test code and no restriction to changed lines: any Bun code containing an in-scope logger call is covered.
Emitted by bun_security_hygiene_detector for any call on a logger receiver (logger/log/_logger/_log/LOG) whose sole argument is a string literal, whether the call is new or pre-existing.

fires: Bun code contains `logger.info("order processed")` with a string literal as the only argument.
A `log.error("...")` call on a logger receiver passes only a string literal, whether newly written or already present.
doesNotFire: A logger call already passes a second argument (context object).
A string-literal-only call on a receiver that is not a logger (not logger/log/_logger/_log/LOG).
Python code, which is governed by the sibling convention coder.logging.structured.

given: Bun code containing a call on a logger receiver (`logger`, `log`, `_logger`, `_log`, `LOG`)
when: the call's sole argument is a string literal
then: Pass a context object as the second argument carrying the fields the line would be searched by; never pass only a bare string literal.
prefer: Ask what you would filter by at 3am during an incident and put those fields in the object, e.g. `logger.info("order processed", { orderId, userId, ms });      // right`.
avoid: Bare-string calls such as `logger.info("order processed");                              // wrong` — greppable and nothing more, at the one moment it matters.
Attaching a token or empty object just to satisfy the detector; the rule asks only that SOME context is attached and cannot judge whether the right fields were chosen.
unless: The call already passes a second argument (not flagged).
The receiver is not a logger (out of scope).
why: A log line's value is realised at exactly one moment: when someone is searching for it during an incident; a bare string can only be grepped, while a line carrying `{ orderId, userId }` can be filtered, grouped and joined to a trace.
verifier_detail: Flag a call on a logger receiver named `logger`, `log`, `_logger`, `_log` or `LOG` whose sole argument is a string literal.
Any call already passing a second argument is not flagged; non-logger receivers are out of scope.
Context object = the second argument carrying the fields a line will be searched by; a JS logger takes an object where a Python one takes `extra=` or kwargs.
The detector checks only that SOME context is attached; it cannot judge whether the right fields were chosen.
